reviews.text: It’s a gorgeous rendering of a classic. Imperfect and messy, but personal and earnest, as well.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: 'Peter Pan & Wendy' is a decent live-action remake stays faithful to the source material as well as its animated predecessor, but that's about it.
reviews.author: Sandeep Sandhu

reviews.text: Faith, trust and pixie dust populate this tale of magic, mystery and swashbuckling sword fights centred around Jude Law’s conflicted Captain Hook
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: As an adult who never bought into those claims that growing up is the greatest adventure, “Peter Pan & Wendy” is poignant and evocative. It serves as an optimistic message to inspire children to meet the challenges of fast-approaching adulthood.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: While Lowery’s Neverland is an enchanting destination ... his idiosyncratic storytelling style seems stifled, as if the studio had promised him a puffy-sleeved pirate shirt and instead strapped him up in a straitjacket.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: A beautiful adaptation of a classic story that blends the book’s mysticism with David Lowery’s knack for the eerie.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text:
David Lowery showcases the best of his ability while crafting a throwback to early 2000’s Fairytale movies mixing depth but also 

Never forgetting the essence of what made the animated feature so magical! 

Count me as a fan!
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Daniel Hart’s score stands out from the other technical components, elevating the several adventure set pieces and transforming Neverland into a truly magical world. The small changes made to the world-building preserve the essence of the original tale.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Lowery doesn’t give us what we think we want in “Peter Pan & Wendy.” ... Instead he gives us something to think about — a variation on a classic story with room to explore and experiment.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The movie is an argument for leaving all the old stories alone if we’re not willing to embrace their weirdness and wrongness. Otherwise, we kill a lot of the odd magic that attracted us to begin with.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: David Lowery should just be put in charge of all of Disney's live-action efforts as he has shown a clear understanding for youthful growing pains and how nostalgia for the past can prevent one from the joys of aging.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Even if this film can’t fully escape its streaming budget, Lowery still manages to make a story that’s been told plenty of times feel fresh.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It's a shame this one didn't get a theatrical release. Lowery's sweeping scenery deserves to be highlighted.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: I would argue this is one of the better efforts compared to the likes of the much more expensive Beauty and the Beast and The Lion King, which is also what I’d expect from director David Lowery.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Even a respected auteur like director David Lowery can’t save Peter Pan & Wendy, yet another bland live-action adaptation of a Disney classic...
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy is a puzzlingly bland take on one of the liveliest children’s stories of all time.
reviews.author: Colleen Morrissey

reviews.text: While Peter Pan and Wendy misses some opportunities to possibly elevate its material, the end result is still pretty entertaining.
reviews.author: Dirk Libbey

reviews.text: Poignant and fanciful.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: There's too much corporate constraints on this film... I think it's time to just cut this franchise loose.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: It's not a totally worthless endeavor but in a world in which dozens of Pan adaptations exist, there's not enough here to separate the movie from its predecessors. If you're going to hire David Lowery, let him cook!
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: Another disappointment among Disney’s increasingly lackluster live action reboots of their classic animated films, “Peter Pan and Wendy” lacks imagination in its re-imagining.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy might be overly saccharine from time to time, but Lowery’s swash-buckling approach to direction makes sure that it’s always light-hearted and fun to watch unfold.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: Even with pirates, a fairy, a Native American princess and a man-eating crocodile, it arrives as oddly unimaginative stuff.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: All talk, no crocodile bite ... The parts just don't add up to a completely engaging trip to Neverland.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: There’s not much here besides something to keep the kids out of your hair for a couple of hours.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: It's great that kids now have a Peter Pan that doesn't lean into antiquated gender roles. As an adventure, though, this version never quite takes flight.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: “Peter Pan & Wendy” is a refreshingly and welcomed adaptation of this story with strong performances all around and fantastic camera work.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: At times, watching this film is like sitting in on a therapy session as a deeply disturbed pirate confronts his repressed memories. All of which will fly over the heads of its intended young audience as surely as Peter does over the rooftops...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: I’m not calling this Peter Pan Gone Wrong, but it’s not as good as that show either.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: While no classic, “Peter Pan & Wendy” is a pretty charming affair, one that should be most appealing to relatively young children.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Another expensive so-so remake...Blessed with a huge budget and some wonderful visual effects, the film looks splendid yet doesn’t come close to capturing the vibrancy and magic of the timeless 1953 film, opting rather for a darker take.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Peter Pan and Wendy is purposefully crafted with care and thoughtfulness, and while it succeeds in expanding the ideas of Wendy, Hook, and Tiger Lily, it’s at the cost of the character of Peter Pan.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Peter Pan and Wendy never masks the redundancy of Disney’s remake formula.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: There’s an alternate universe where David Lowery made a Peter Pan movie with ultimate freedom, and imagining that makes watching Peter Pan & Wendy a little bittersweet.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: There is swashbuckling and the ticking crocodile and Smee, but the narrative always feels perfunctory and inert possibly because there’s just no spark between any of the characters, least of all Wendy and Peter, who is portrayed as a sulky kind of chap.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy shows the usefulness of the concept of the Disney live-action remake; it updates the racial and gender politics of the original 1953 animated film while also drawing further from the story upon which that story was based.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: In the end, Peter Pan & Wendy is a fantasy film that undercuts its own sense of wonder.
reviews.author: Tyler Smith

reviews.text: The Disney brand will bring broad audiences to Peter Pan & Wendy, but they might be surprised by the broody aesthetic and contemplative messages of Lowery's adaptation, not to mention its alternate ending.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: Both visually and narratively uninteresting, Peter Pan & Wendy is another forgettable live-action remake from Disney, and further proof that live-action versions of animated movies are just not on par.
reviews.author: Joey Rambles

reviews.text: Grinds all of the fantastical elements out as much as can possibly be done for a story about using magical dust to fly
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy is visually spectacular and tells the story we all know about the boy who could fly. It’s one of the better of these Disney retreads and that is ultimately enough.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Of course there’s swashbuckling derring-do and a giant crocodile too, but Law gets to infuse the panto appeal of Hook with genuine pathos.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: [Peter Pan & Wendy] is impressive at times but there is also the feeling that, once again, the corporate machine "domesticated" and distilled everything original and daring... Not everything that dazzles is great cinema. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: While it looks great, sounds great, and at times plays great, it doesn’t have much of a lasting effect.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The themes of childhood wonder, imagination and friendship all play out in a predictably mundane storyline. While Peter Pan and Wendy is worth streaming, this new re-telling of the well-worn fable may not make you want to crow.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: “Peter Pan and Wendy” is the perfect title as Wendy shares the spotlight with Peter and at times outshines him due to her broad screen time and her determined performance.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: While I appreciated certain aspects of David Lowery’s production, “Peter Pan & Wendy” was a chore.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Children too might object to the film’s seriousness — although it comes with a sense of wonder and plenty of swashbuckling action scenes.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: The movie is entertaining and has a professional polish; but it’s also very safe.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: It’s an expertly made movie, but one in which the lifeblood has been mostly drained.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: It’s bogged down by a slog of unimagination that spends too much time sucking the life and magic out of a story set in a magical world. Maybe that’s part of the point, but shouldn’t we also want to go to Neverland, even if only for a moment?
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: Lowery has been talking about mortality, growing up and legacy, so he fits perfectly here. The only aspect of the film that I didn’t love is that the scale feels so small.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: One of the better live-action adaptations of the fantasy classic. David Lowery injects enough visual splendor within the world and interesting dynamics between the characters to warrant a view. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Lowery's version of this well-known story plays it pretty safe, but the film does manage to tap into the magical feeling of Barrie's classic novel and give its audience a fresh experience of wonder.
reviews.author: Patrick Hicks

reviews.text: As Lowery's marvelous “Pete’s Dragon” accomplished, if to greater, more striking success, “Peter Pan & Wendy” is rooted not in envisioning how it might look to fly straight on till morning but in the melancholy of realizing that's a two-way journey.
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: It’s a familiar story, but in its details, the film suffers from an odd mix of overcorrection and half-hearted ness.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: David Lowery has mounted a film that is very much grown up.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: It is evident that David Lowery understands this world, but the film needs even more of his creativity. Hook and Wendy are standouts, while other characters aren’t great. Overall, the film has enough magic and fun to suffice.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: One can appreciate Lowery’s sensitive handling of problematic material while still finding the overall results wanting.
reviews.author: Andrew Dignan

reviews.text: The film suffers in its familiarity, & the kinda modern emphasis on relationships over action, BUT the special effects are great, especially during the famous flying sequences, and the cast is game to handle the changes and the legend. Jim Gaffigan Smee!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: A little more pixie dust, please.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: When detractors decry Disney for cannibalizing IP for profit, they could point to Peter Pan & Wendy, a live-action recreation of a classic movie that mercilessly bleeds life out of its iconic characters and passion out of its heralded helmer.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: …Whatever you want to believe in Peter Pan or not, Lowery’s Peter Pan & Wendy is probably the smartest of the live-action Disney films to date, jammed with irreverent sea-shanties and briskly told over a commendably brief 90 minutes…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy is another example of realism ruining creativity. From Hook’s drab appearance to a lack of colour to boring action, it has no personality. It’s not the worst of the Disney live-actions, but the studio is losing touch with its own magic.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: P.J. Hogan’s Peter Pan remains the champ, but Lowery has made a solid contender that actually improves upon the animated version.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: A gorgeous, visually interesting film that explores its setpieces with love: of filmmaking; of visual storytelling; of the source material’s fantastic potential.
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: Still packed with the wonder of the original, but it struggles against the modern necessities of an update of the story.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Jude Law makes for a grimacing and  scary Captain Hook and Jim Gaffigan is fun as Mr Smee... If you are in the mood for a take on Peter Pan it's perfectly enjoyable version but nothing more.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy is proof that it isn't too difficult to make a good live action version of a Disney Classic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy takes too long to fly
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Mr Barrie’s enduring bedtime yarn is ripe for an awesome cinematic adaptation. Sadly, this isn’t it.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: By the time the woolly pirates burst into their second rousing sea shanty, our minds begin to liken the Jolly Roger to the philosophical paradox of Theseus’s ship: How many planks can you swap out while still claiming it’s the real deal?
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: It tries so hard to reconcile its obligatory beats with Lowery’s go-deeper-than-you-have-to storytelling that it ends up feeling like an incongruous mix of both.
reviews.author: Hayden Mears

reviews.text: If Lowery had reinvented Peter Pan, much like he did with Pete’s Dragon, a much better movie would have likely been the result. Instead, there’s a front-loaded fealty to the traditional interpretation of the story that’s pretty boring.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: In spite of [Lowery's] numerous hints toward a refreshing take, the light of this particular promise remains mostly obscured.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Still, for everyone else, this is yet another exercise in mediocrity that could have been so much better. If Tinkerbell’s life really depended on audiences clapping to save her, she would be D.O.A.
reviews.author: Alex Maidy

reviews.text: In live-action, it's a lot harder to buy a child beating up adult pirates. The grown-up actors have to let Peter win, like parents do when they play games with their small children.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Smarter and way more magical than Spielberg’s Hook, P. J. Hogan’s Peter Pan or Joe Wright’s Pan, this version, when it gets off the ground, soars.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Lowery’s Peter Pan & Wendy stands out as one of Disney’s best live-action remake in a decade.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy isn’t a complete failure, but nor does this return to Neverland pass that test; rather, it’s another case of a Disney production that -- unlike the beloved and venerable story that inspired it -- never truly takes flight.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The ambition and the beauty of the film is undeniable. Peter Pan & Wendy is definitely not your father’s favorite family film. It distinctly hews an independent path to its intended conclusion.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: The production goes to great strides to humanize the characters and give them a modern perspective, yet doesn't have any problems using moments of violence in an outdated context. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy gets a marginal recommendation because even though the film doesn’t soar to adventurous new heights, it still manages to escape the dated shadow of its early predecessors.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Peter Pan and Wendy upends expectations by showing directorial vision and narrative ambition. It’s fun and thoughtful with equal measure.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: David Lowery isn’t trying too hard to reinvent the wheel with Peter Pan & Wendy but it’s not a total copycat knock off like the recent Pinocchio remake
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The 1st half of the movie is horrible, but the 2nd half is so fascinating it's worth your time. Lowery offers an incredibly sophisticated take on Peter Pan, when he's interested. This is a story about Wendy and Captain Hook, with Peter largely left out.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: I’m convinced David Lowery is the only one who can manufacture real emotion and make these movies look like something other than hogwash.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Disappointingly, Lowery opts for a fairly straightforward remake of a story we've seen dozens of times before instead of something more imaginative like we know he's capable of. Still gorgeous visually with a great score, and Ever Anderson is a highlight.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: By changing elements—for legitimate reasons—it becomes a diverse coming-of-age tale, but it also loses a lot of what made its predecessors memorable and magical.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: There are rare glimpses of brilliance in Peter Pan & Wendy that hint at a bold take on this beloved story, but those moments are far too infrequent. The rest of the film is so stale and shallow that it’s hard to truly call this something new.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: One of the year’s best films, David Lowery’s “Peter Pan and Wendy” provides a more adult, melancholy take on J.M. Barrie’s seminal tale.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy bucks the trend of bad live action updates of Disney’s animated films, sprinkling just the right amount of fairy dust on the story to make it feel new again.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: When compared to the narrative catastrophes of most of the other live-action Disney remakes, Peter Pan & Wendy seems to have found more success than it had any right to.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: ...other than feeling like a necessary update to rid itself of negative historical stereotypes, "Peter Pan & Wendy" feels flat.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Lowery's tone is perhaps a little too gloomy, too existential to be appreciated by kids of all ages. But the precocious ones eager to grow up fast might just hold this one close.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: David Lowery has taken a beloved fairy tale and reconfigured it with charm, artistry, and compassion.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: The changes within Peter Pan and Wendy ... remain either superficial ... or ... entirely beneath the surface of a too-familiar narrative.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Lowery's Peter Pan becomes a meditation on the universal tension between the recklessness of youth and the caution of age; a young person’s wild resentfulness of authority and an elder’s crotchety adherence to norms.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: The updates to the cast and story are very much welcome without feeling forced or overbearing.
reviews.author: Catherine Gonzales

reviews.text: Peter Pan and Wendy has its moments, but a frustrating lack of imagination by Lowery holds it back from reaching the heights that Neverland deserves. Instead, it’s a drab and dry reimagining that has apparent poignant moments that are half-baked...
reviews.author: Swara Salih

reviews.text: Lowery, for what it’s worth, does attempt to add depth with the thornier character dynamics and his trademark ethereal directorial flairs, but Peter Pan & Wendy ends up coming off a listless attempt to recapture a magic that was never there to begin with.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy is going to surprise a lot of people with just how good it is. It’s a shame though, because it could have been perfect with a few small tweaks.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: David Lowery’s Disney+ live-action re-imagining barely takes flight.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy does just about everything you wouldn’t want an adaptation of J.M. Barrie’s story to do.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: It's caught between the mature treatment Lowery likely had in mind and the Disney-friendly imperatives that make Peter Pan & Wendy watery.
reviews.author: Matthew Jacobs

reviews.text: Visually hearty but ultimately thin.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Lowery’s second Disney remake, Peter Pan & Wendy, recreates Peter Pan—a story that has already had its fair share of remakes over the years—and, like with Pete’s Dragon, manages to breathe new life into a story we’ve already heard countless times.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: By softening the story, Lowery has diminished it and made something that - while  pretty to look at and entertaining enough for family night around the TV - loses something deeper.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: While Disney's Peter Pan & Wendy is strangely lacking some magic, it is saved by a scene-stealing Jude Law, its young cast, and a deeper narrative.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: On its own, Peter Pan & Wendy is enjoyable enough.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: Lowery may be a massive talent, but his sensibilities feel wasted in a muted landscape with such little personality.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: Disney’s latest live action updating of one of their animated classics, Peter Pan & Wendy, is, like a lot of their other efforts in a similar vein, good looking, underwhelming, and unnecessary.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Lowery’s movie, while steeped in nostalgia itself, is also about the tragedy of living in a world without it.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: An exquisitely balanced mix of visual spectacle and grounded, intimate moments, buttressed by uniformly strong, naturalistic performances from a talented cast. ... Should be considered a worthy, worthwhile addition to any streaming diet.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: It finds ways to restore a little magic to the tale, and it’s newly focused on the emotional health of the characters, which keeps it interesting.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The new Disney+ iteration of the classic tale doesn't add much new to the Neverland mythology, but it's a rousing, action-filled caper that should please the kids.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: ANYTHING is an improvement over the 1953 stereotypes...Maybe Peter Pan has grown up a little bit - but finally in a good way. Relatable, but still a live-action straight-to-streaming meh.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: While the script undoubtedly delivers this nuance, especially as the story plays out across the final act, it is Jude Law’s performance that elevates it. His magnetic chemistry with the camera makes the film exceedingly rewatchable.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: For a tale that’s been adapted [so often], Peter Pan & Wendy was crying out for an infusion of [David] Lowery’s Green Knight magic. Unfortunately, he’s delivered a less-than-serviceable remake that’s both undercooked and repetitive at the same time.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Despite the fact that it trades in a dogged familiarity, this magical story still retains some spark.
reviews.author: Nikki Baughan

reviews.text: David Lowery's desire to bring the human experience to the forefront of every story he tells is as present here as it is in any of his other films, this one just comes with a gaggle of Lost Boys and a little bit of pixie dust.
reviews.author: Charlie Ridgely

reviews.text: Kids will eat it all up, as they have been doing for well over a century, and Lowery’s not necessarily necessary retelling does nothing to harm the impact of a story that itself is forever young.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Lowery invests the whole of it with a mood both grave and warm, with serious dramatic stakes.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: ... An adaptation that, for all its well-executed ideas, feels a little too keen to grow up.
reviews.author: Ben Travis

reviews.text: This version of the fairytale grounds the fundamental wistfulness of the original tale with empathetic backstories and takes care to remedy the original’s overt racism and latent sexism.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: It’s all done crisply and simply enough for an eight-year-old to easily follow along with the film’s train of thought, and movingly enough to turn any adults on the sofa beside them to a sniffling heap.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Infused with bounding energy but little meaningful invention, it climbs to only modest heights, weighed down by its inability to add much to the iconic legend.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: A bizarrely disjointed and patchy experience that lurches forward in clunky set pieces, consistently foregrounding surface details that have little impact on the brittle underlying narrative.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: One of the most visually stunning trips to Neverland ever recorded on film, featuring a cast of gifted young actors and reliable veterans who seem born to the roles.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: In Disney’s haste to adapt more of its precious IP, the studio has sublimated another classic into mere “content,” to be swept downstream and forgotten.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: While the results are a little uneven narratively, the breathless action, stellar performances, and beautiful compositions carry the story to rousing heights.
reviews.author: Brian Roan

reviews.text: [Lowery's] 21st century take on this age-old tale flies high and sticks the landing because it stays true to the moral of 119-year-old story: Accepting that everything changes is the first step towards discovering that nothing is truly lost.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Lowery doesn’t stray too far outside the lines — this is still a Disney movie based on a beloved family property — but he also doesn’t shy away from mining a familiar tale for meta commentary. Far from deconstruction, it’s heartfelt and introspective.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: While Peter Pan & Wendy isn’t as carefully crafted nor as emotionally transcendent as Pete’s Dragon, it still represents a solid “one for them” paycheque gig.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: The result is tasteful, artisanal, melancholy and doomed. Children everywhere will squint a little before asking if they can see The Super Mario Bros Movie again.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: While one can appreciate Lowery’s decision to create rather than simply replicate, [the movie,] more meditative than magical,...struggles to find its own footing and ultimately stumbles, winding up neither very engaging nor particularly insightful.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: While Lowery’s vision reliably entertains, it lacks that little something extra, that sprinkle of pixie dust, to be truly memorable.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy is a grand family adventure film. Lowery’s vision has a sweet message for kids about the fragile nature of relationships.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: 'Peter Pan & Wendy' is a meaningful bit of cinematic poetry that’s as vivid as its characters’ imaginations. Lowery sprinkles the classic tale with his own batch of fairy dust that’s monumentally satisfying and should see more stories from this Neverland.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: This isn't a movie that will thrill those who love the book or previous versions of the story. But if you're looking for an easy watch – and an hour and a half of Jude Law brilliance – it's definitely worth a try.
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: A respectful retelling that finds time to hit all the iconic moments, while adding meaningful story expansion. At 100mins it’s brisk and feverish. Action set pieces are terrific, flying sequences dizzying.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: Bless his heart, David Lowery has not forgotten the sensation and formative power found in the analog brands of fantasy.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: In reimagining the story in live-action, Peter Pan & Wendy elevates its heroines in the best way possible.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Peter Pan & Wendy sees David Lowery Bring his unique vision to the classic children's tale.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: In an attempt to add some depth, writer/director David Lowery diverges from J.M. Barrie’s original tale in some significant ways, touching on darker, previously unexplored elements of the story. The results are a mixed bag.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: An unbalanced attempt...with enough battles, humor, and exciting sequences to wake up the kids who fell asleep during the quieter moments. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Tinker Bell (Yara Shahidi) can’t sprinkle any fairy dust on this cold, watered-down version of the magical tale.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Filled with childlike wonder, David Lowery’s Neverland is a magical place that’s sometimes a bit too fixated on its infamous villain.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

synopsis: Based on J. M. Barrie's novel "Peter and Wendy" and inspired by the 1953 animated classic, "Peter Pan & Wendy" is the timeless tale of a young girl who, defying her parents' wishes to attend boarding school, travels with her two younger brothers to the magical Neverland. There, she meets a boy who refuses to grow up, a tiny fairy and an evil pirate captain, and they soon find themselves on a thrilling and dangerous adventure far, far away from their family and the comforts of home.
